title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Permissive Withdrawal - Arbitrary Reasons
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A paralegal decides they want to withdraw from a difficult client's file simply because they "no longer like the client's personality," even though the client pays on time and follows all instructions. Is this an ethically valid ground for withdrawal?
options: Yes, a paralegal can withdraw from any file for any reason at any time.
Yes, if the paralegal gives the client 24 hours notice.
No, a paralegal may only withdraw for good cause and with reasonable notice; personal dislike without a breakdown in the relationship is not sufficient.
No, unless the paralegal finds replacement counsel first.
questions.explain: Rule 8.02 requires that permissive withdrawal only occur for "good cause" and upon reasonable notice. Simply disliking a cooperative, paying client's personality is not generally considered good cause. Good cause includes a severe breakdown in communication, loss of trust, or non-payment.
